title: Map to the blow-up chart of the extended ideal
statement:
Let $f:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $I\subseteq A$ an ideal and $a\in I$. Put $J=IB=(f(x):x\in I)\subseteq B$ and $b=f(a)\in J$. Use the chart algebras $A[I/a]\subseteq A_a$ and $B[J/b]\subseteq B_b$ of [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], and put $C_a(A,B,I)=B\otimes_A A[I/a]$ as in [def-nagata-strict-transform-basechange-chart-ring]. Define $\sigma_a:C_a(A,B,I)\to B[J/b]$ as follows: extend $A\xrightarrow{f}B\to B_b$ to $A_a\to B_b$, restrict this map to $A[I/a]\to B[J/b]$, and take the tensor-product homomorphism with the structural map $B\to B[J/b]$. Thus $\sigma_a$ is a homomorphism of $B$-algebras and on pure tensors of chart generators it satisfies
$$\sigma_a\bigl(y\otimes(x/a)\bigr)=y\,f(x)/b\qquad(y\in B,\ x\in I).$$
The localization and tensor-product maps used in this construction are those of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] and [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property].

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property] to $R=A$, the element $a$, the target $P=B_b$, and the composite $A\xrightarrow{f}B\to B_b$. Its value at $a$ is $b/1$, a unit with inverse $1/b$ by the localization relations. It gives a ring map $\lambda:A_a\to B_b$ with $\lambda(x/a^n)=f(x)/b^n$. On coefficients it is the structural map from $A$, so it is an $A$-algebra map. This constructs the first map without choosing representatives of chart elements.

source.place: Tag 00CP, proposition-universal-property-localization; applied to the powers of a

proof.text: By [def-nagata-blowup-chart-ring], $A[I/a]$ is generated as an $A$-algebra by $x/a$ for $x\in I$. The inverse image $\lambda^{-1}(B[J/b])$ is an $A$-subalgebra of $A_a$: sums and products stay in it because $\lambda$ is a ring map, and it contains all coefficients. Each generator lies in it since $\lambda(x/a)=f(x)/b$ and $f(x)\in J$. Hence it contains the generated subalgebra $A[I/a]$. Restriction of $\lambda$ therefore defines $g:A[I/a]\to B[J/b]$ as an $A$-algebra map. This is just the defining smallest-subalgebra property, not a new comparison theorem.

source.place: definition of sigma_a by the images of chart generators; elementary expansion of the generated-subalgebra definition

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property], clause (2), with base ring $A$, factor algebras $B$ and $A[I/a]$, target $B[J/b]$, and maps the structural map $s:B\to B[J/b]$ and $g$. Both are $A$-algebra maps since $g$ restricts to $s\circ f$ on $A$. It yields $h:B\otimes_A A[I/a]\to B[J/b]$, $h(y\otimes c)=s(y)g(c)$. In particular $h(y\otimes1)=s(y)$, so $h$ is a $B$-algebra map for the left-factor $B$-structure on the ring of [def-nagata-strict-transform-basechange-chart-ring]. Define $\sigma_a=h$. Substituting $c=x/a$ gives precisely $y f(x)/b$. Clause (3) gives uniqueness from the two factor maps; thus no choices enter the construction.

blueprint_notes.text:
**Status.** Bypassed by the formalized route: the strict transform is
supplied by the API of
`WeilConjectures/Compactification/StrictTransform.lean` —
`AlgebraicGeometry.strictTransform`, its closed immersion
`AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.IdealSheafData.isClosedImmersion_pullbackLift_blowup_comap`,
and the pullback square
`AlgebraicGeometry.isPullback_strictTransformOpen` — so the
strict-transform chart rings and their cocycle are never assembled by hand.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $J=IB\subseteq B$, let $b$ be the image of $a$ in $B$, and write
$B[J/b]$ for the corresponding chart ring. Define

$$
\sigma_a\colon C_a(A,B,I)\longrightarrow B[J/b]
$$

on pure tensors and chart generators by

$$
\sigma_a\bigl(y\otimes(x/a)\bigr)=y\,\overline x/b.
$$

Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-localization-away-universal-property (a Mathlib leaf) gives lambda:A_a→B_b because f(a)/1=b/1 is a unit; the formula and the A-linearity check out. Step 2 is elementary: the preimage of B[J/b] under lambda is an A-subalgebra containing every generator x/a, since lambda(x/a)=f(x)/b and f(x)∈J; it never cancels a. Step 3: lem-weil-pbc-algebra-tensor-pushout-universal-property (2)/(3) is applied to s:B→B[J/b] and g, which agree on A. This gives a B-algebra map with the formula, unique by clause (3).
